final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the key missing predicates: no approved risk acceptance, no remediation evidence, no completed disclosure, and no final legal determination. The response usefully narrows the argument by distinguishing general launch readiness from the named-segment disclosure issue, but that is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new evidence. That distinction is not enough for compliant_with_caveats here, because the unresolved issue is not merely how to word certification; it is whether a required policy condition for a material limitation affecting a named launch use case was satisfied before launch. Public guidance on documentation and monitoring can support governance posture, but it cannot replace the internal policy requirement. On this record, caveated certification may be a plausible business posture, but it is not shown to be policy-compliant.
remaining_concerns: The affected segment is named in two agency grant commitments, so the limitation remains material despite the 5% traffic framing.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so the disclosure predicate is still unresolved.
No admissible evidence shows the 1.3 percentage-point gap was remediated before launch for the named grant-commitment segment.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance exists for this limitation before launch.
Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance do not satisfy the separate internal policy predicate for a material named-segment limitation.
